Your workout notebook. No ads, no tracking and truly free. Your data stays on your phone and, if you prefer, in your own cloud too.

In Train, pick your routine and tap Start. Enter the weight and reps for each set and tick it with ✓. Ticking it starts the rest timer and I’ll let you know when it’s over. Tap what you did last time and it’s copied over.
A week counts when you complete every routine in your program. It can’t be ticked by hand: you earn your streak by training.
Log your body weight in Profile and you’ll see your rank for each muscle, from Iron to Diamond, with your next goal. New records come with the spark.
I help you keep track, but I’m not a doctor or a coach. If you have an injury or a health condition, see a professional before you start. If you feel pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, stop.
You can export a backup whenever you want. If you connect your GitHub (optional), your workouts are saved automatically to a private file in your account.

string-array.name: como_se_calcula_pasos
string-array.item: 1. For each exercise I take your best set and estimate your one-rep max (Epley formula).

2. I compare it with Fogón’s strength table, scaled to your body weight. Bench press, squat and deadlift were calibrated with thousands of powerlifting meet results (OpenPowerlifting); the other exercises are estimated from those three.

3. Ranks: Iron (starting out) · Bronze (beginner) · Silver (novice) · Gold (intermediate) · Platinum (advanced, the level of someone starting to compete) · Diamond (elite, stronger than ~3 in 4 competitors). Each rank has 3 divisions: III, II and I.
4. Each muscle’s rank is the average of its 2 best exercises, and the overall rank is the average of all your muscles.
5. For dumbbells, log the weight of one dumbbell. On machines and cables the rank is approximate, because the marked weight varies between machines. Planks, raises and bodyweight lunges don’t count.

El Forzudo is a workout notebook, not medical advice. The routines, goals and ranks are general guides that don’t know your health. If you have an injury, an illness or haven’t trained in a long time, see a health professional before you start. If you feel pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, stop. string-array.name: respuestas
string-array.item: The drawings come from Everkinetic, a freely licensed bank of exercise illustrations, and all its figures are male. We found no free illustrations with female figures. We tried generating them with artificial intelligence, but they weren’t at the same level or in the same style, and we’d rather not ship something half-done. The exercise and the muscle it works are the same for everyone. If anyone wants to draw the female versions under a free license, they’re welcome.
We only use drawings with a clear license, and those exercises don’t have one yet. They’ll come in an update.

The photos the app used came from a bank that presented itself as free, but they were actually photos taken from the internet without their owners’ permission. So they were replaced with clearly licensed drawings.

Each muscle group has its own color, the same throughout the app: the patch on the drawing marks the muscle being worked. The drawing’s shadow tells the area: pink for the upper body, yellow for the arms and blue for the legs.

From Fogón’s own table, calibrated with real powerlifting meet results (OpenPowerlifting, public domain). The other exercises are estimated from bench press, squat and deadlift, so on machines the rank is approximate.
No. Everything is stored on the phone. Only if you connect your own GitHub are your workouts copied to a private file in your account.
